steps.what: State the audience, site and question
Collect the signed design points
Draft the proposal from those points

loop.input: signed design points and the proposal sections
loop.check: Every recommendation cites a signed design point id
loop.stop: One draft; drop a sentence with no point id
loop.why_not_simpler: How the design is argued for this audience is not a lookup

steps.what: Present the proposal to staff
Sign the presented proposal version
File the presented proposal version

tasks.design: The service owner states the audience, the site and the question. Signed design points are taken from {DOCS}. A bounded proposal cites only those point ids. The architect presents it, then signs the version that was actually presented, and that version is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Slides were rebuilt from old decks, so a sentence could not be tied to the design that was current.
tasks.enabler_now: A design point id can be stored with the recommendation that uses it.
tasks.still_hard: How to argue the design for this audience, and what to change after questions, stays in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The architect presents the proposal and signs the version that leaves the room.

ambition.what: Staff who were not in the room can read the signed proposal

tasks.altitude: Less rewriting of slides. The architect can refuse to file a sentence that cites no design point. The presentation stays.

reach.task: Use the filed proposal version with the business
reach.learn: Which design points were presented and which were dropped after questions

evidence.claim: A design proposal in a mid-size firm is a document plus a presentation. The sentences can cite design points. The room cannot.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong, so a recommendation cites a design point id rather than a filled column.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends when the presented version is filed. A customer receives that version through the service owner.

Input contract: audience, site, question, design point id, design version. Producer of the question is the service owner. Producer of the points is the signed design. A sentence with no point id is dropped.
Use the document store's own versions before custom code. The presentation is not treated as saved. The meeting prior fits that room time.
unknowns: Whether customers may see the full design or only the proposal.
Who presents when the architect is absent.
research_questions: What share of proposal sentences cannot be tied to a design point?
How often does the filed version differ from the draft that was presented?

already_counted.description: Architect rewrites weak proposal sentences before the room
Presentation time stays with the architect

incremental.description: Update proposal sections when a new design point type appears
Service owners resubmit a brief that has no question

approvals.approved_version: proposal version signed after this presentation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the design points are not signed fields, so the draft is rewritten and the presentation itself is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Optimize network designs in the drawing file

steps.what: Open the current drawing file
Compare drawing devices with inventory
Optimize paths on the network design
Draft a note of moved device ids

loop.input: moved device ids and the inventory
loop.check: Every device id on the note is in the inventory
loop.stop: One pass; drop an id the inventory does not hold
loop.why_not_simpler: Why a path moved is a design judgement, not a name match

steps.what: Sign this drawing file version
Read the signed drawing file

tasks.design: The architect opens the drawing file in {DOCS} and optimizes paths on the screen. A side-by-side view shows device ids against the {OPS_SYSTEM} inventory. A bounded note may cite only ids the inventory holds. The architect signs the drawing file version. The file is not applied to live devices from here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Device names on the drawing and in the inventory drifted apart, so a note could not tell a real move from a label mismatch.
tasks.enabler_now: A device id can be compared between the drawing file and the inventory.
tasks.still_hard: Where a path should go, and how much redundancy the site needs, is still the architect's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The architect moves the paths and signs the drawing file version.

ambition.what: Update the drawing when a device id changes, not only at the next project

tasks.altitude: Name mismatches surface before the review. The path judgement stays on the screen. The architect can refuse to sign a file that cites an unknown device.

reach.task: Build from the signed drawing file version
reach.learn: Which device ids moved and which version was signed

evidence.claim: Optimizing a network drawing is specialist screen work. A name check is not the design.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong, so the drawing file itself is not produced that way.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so the drawing file is not applied to live devices by an unattended agent.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends when the drawing file version is signed. Applying it to live devices is a later change.

Input contract: device id, site, link id, drawing version. Producer of the drawing is the architect. Producer of the device list is the inventory. An id the inventory does not hold is dropped from the note and marked on the drawing.
The screen prior fits. The drawing package stays; this design does not replace it. The prior that standard software does not fit is accepted. Compare ids in the existing inventory before custom code.
unknowns: Whether every device on the drawing has an inventory id.
Who may sign a drawing when the architect is absent.
research_questions: What share of drawing labels has no inventory id?
How often does a signed drawing change again before build?

already_counted.description: Path judgement on the drawing stays with the architect
Architect edits the change note before signing

incremental.description: Keep the device-id comparison aligned when the inventory adds a field

approvals.approved_version: drawing file version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes device names on the drawing do not match inventory ids, so the note stays empty and the path judgement is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit vendors and study technology changes

steps.what: Choose the visit or the journal
Add the journal issue to the list
Visit the vendor or attend training
Present the product at the visit
Note what would change a design
Sign the technology note version

tasks.design: The architect chooses a vendor visit, a training session or a journal issue, and files the issue title on a list in {DOCS}. The visit or the session stays in person with the vendor engineer. Afterwards the architect writes what would change a design and signs that note. A feed does not replace the visit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes from visits were loose pages, so a later design could not tell which visit a recommendation came from.
tasks.enabler_now: A visit date, a vendor name and a journal title can be stored as a short list.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a product is worth a change to this network is still a judgement made after being there.
tasks.human_edge: The architect chooses what is worth the time and what would actually change a design.
tasks.altitude: The reading list is easier to find. The visit, the conference and the training stay. Nothing is bought or changed from the note alone.

reach.task: Answer the question list at the visit
reach.learn: Which products the architect asked about and which note was signed afterwards

evidence.claim: Keeping up with network technology in a mid-size firm is a visit, a conference or a journal. A reading list does not replace being there.
Digest [S7] and [S8] describe a managed detection service that speeds investigation for mid-size firms, while analysts still decide. That service does not stand in for a vendor visit or a conference.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed technology note. It does not select a product for purchase or change the live network.
Input contract: visit date, vendor name, journal title, question, design area. Producer is the architect. A note that names no visit or no issue is not filed.
The meeting prior fits the visit and the conference. Those hours stay. The list uses the document store's own folder before custom code.
unknowns: Whether journal access is already paid for.
research_questions: How many visits last year produced a note that changed a design?
What share of journal issues is never opened again?

already_counted.description: Time at the visit or the session stays with the architect
Architect's judgement of what would change a design

incremental.description: Add a journal title or a visit to the list on return

approvals.approved_version: technology note signed after this visit or issue

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the visit and the conference stay as they are. The reading list is the only lighter step, and it is not counted as a substitute for being there.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Name the project rows the report needs
Sign which rows the report keeps
Configure the project reporting view
Refresh the report from signed rows
Draft commentary from variance rows

loop.input: variance rows from the signed report
loop.check: Every project id in the commentary is on the variance list
loop.stop: One draft; delete a sentence with no project id
loop.why_not_simpler: The story of a late milestone is not a fixed sentence

steps.what: Sign this period's report commentary

tasks.design: The project controller names project id, milestone, date and amount. The architect signs which rows the report keeps. A {BI} view on {PROJECT} refreshes those rows. Commentary in {DOCS} may cite only project ids that are off the line, and the architect signs that period's commentary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each pack was pasted together from sheets, so a reader could not tell which row definition was current.
tasks.enabler_now: Project id, milestone date and amount can refresh on a schedule once the row list is signed.
tasks.still_hard: What a late milestone means for the network work is still a comment a person must sign.
tasks.human_edge: The architect chooses the rows and signs the commentary for the period.

ambition.what: Look at a variance the week it appears, not only in the monthly pack

tasks.altitude: The pack stops being rebuilt. The architect can refuse a commentary line that cites no project id, and still writes the hard weeks.

reach.task: Keep the project rows the report is signed to use
reach.learn: Which rows are in the report and which commentary version was signed

evidence.claim: A project report in a mid-size firm repeats the same columns. The commentary on a bad week does not.
Digest [S23] says a works council is consulted before staff monitoring. This report stays on the project id, not on a named employee.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong, so commentary cites a project id rather than a filled column.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task is the reporting system and this period's commentary, not a change to the project dates themselves.
Input contract: project id, milestone, planned date, actual date, amount. Producer is the project controller. A row with no project id is left out of the refresh.
Use the project tool's own report before custom code. Hours are not shown by person, so works-council consent for staff monitoring is not triggered.
unknowns: Which projects have no milestone date.
Who signs the commentary when the architect is absent.
research_questions: What share of projects is missing a milestone date?
How often does the signed row list change in a quarter?

already_counted.description: Architect's choice of which rows the report keeps
Architect edits commentary before signing the period

incremental.description: Adjust the report view when a new milestone type is added
Project controller repairs rows that have no project id

approvals.approved_version: report row list signed for this reporting system
the same signed report row list
commentary signed for this report period

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes project rows are incomplete, so the refresh is partial and the commentary is still written in full. The decision on a bad week is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The architect still draws the network, visits vendors and presents the design, and stops rebuilding proposal text, reading lists and status packs.
reach: Service owners receive the proposal version that was actually signed after the presentation.
Network engineers build from the signed drawing file, not a marked-up copy.
Vendor engineers get a question list before the visit.
Project controllers read a report that refreshes from signed rows.
skills_to_grow: Cite only signed design points in a proposal.
Keep the drawing judgement, and check device names against the inventory.
Write a visit note as what would change a design.
Define report rows once, then let the extract repeat.
role.ambitious_version: Every presented proposal, drawing file and project report names the version that was signed.
